prompt:
Build a comprehensive personal replacement for Dorik in an empty repository. You must use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and support static export where appropriate. Do not offer alternative technology stacks. 

The application must be a versatile, drag-and-drop visual website builder tailored to quickly design, manage, and publish responsive websites without coding. 

First, implement a robust visual drag-and-drop editor. The editor should provide a canvas where users can easily compose layouts using a rich library of pre-built UI blocks (e.g., hero sections, features, testimonials, pricing, FAQ, and footers). Users should be able to drag these blocks onto the canvas, reorder them, and visually edit text and images inline. The design system must be constrained, utilizing design tokens for typography, colors, and spacing to ensure a professional aesthetic. Provide live previews of the site across desktop, tablet, and mobile breakpoints, and highlight responsive issues.

Second, incorporate lightweight AI capabilities. Integrate an interface where users can provide a natural language prompt to generate a base layout structure. Additionally, provide an inline AI text generation tool that helps users write SEO-optimized copy directly within the editor. 

Third, include a lightweight Content Management System (CMS) to handle dynamic collections such as blog posts. The CMS should allow users to create and manage structured content that can be dynamically injected into templates. Provide basic features for managing gated content or simple memberships, keeping it local and lightweight.

Fourth, implement comprehensive site settings and SEO management. Allow users to configure metadata, Open Graph tags, titles, and descriptions for every page.

All user data and project configurations must be stored locally in SQLite. Provide a mechanism to export the project state as a portable JSON file, and support importing. The final step of the builder should generate a clean static Next.js output directory ready for deployment.

Ensure the app has clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states. Add robust input validation and handle local image uploads safely with responsive optimization.

Put secrets in `.env`, ship `.env.example`, and never commit credentials. Provide a detailed `README.md` containing setup instructions, architecture, data location, and backup steps. Write unit tests for core transformations and one end-to-end happy path test simulating creating and publishing a site. 

Do not include SaaS billing, advanced telemetry, or a plugin marketplace. Make the first run work locally with one documented command. Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
